# Status

This is a **Candidate Specification — Discussion Draft** for a Rincoin
hard-fork consensus change. Publication does not imply adoption. The
specification, reference implementation, tests, activation plan, service
readiness, and chain-identification decisions remain under review.

**Document version 1.0 · Public-review date 2026-08-07**

The key words **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **SHOULD**, **SHOULD NOT**, and **MAY** in
this document are to be interpreted as described in
RFC 2119 and RFC 8174 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals
[@bradner1997rfc2119; @leiba2017rfc8174].

# Scope

This specification defines only the maximum permitted block subsidy at and
after block height 840,000 under candidate S5/b.

It does not change:

- prior blockchain history or the validity of blocks below height 840,000;
- existing UTXOs or ownership claims;
- RinHash or its parameters;
- Dark Gravity Wave v3;
- transaction format or signature rules;
- transaction-fee accounting;
- any unrelated consensus rule.

Transaction replay, network separation, release deployment, and service
migration require separate decisions. They are not solved by this subsidy rule.

# Definitions

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| Activation height $H$ | `840000` |
| Phase anchor $A$ | `630000` |
| Long reward epoch length $L$ | `2100000` blocks |
| Base unit | $10^{-8}$ RIN; `1 RIN = 100000000` base units |
| Base subsidy $R$ | `625000000` base units, or `6.25000000 RIN` |
| Post-activation phase index $n$ | $\left\lfloor(h-A)/L\right\rfloor$ for height $h\geq H$ |
| Maximum permitted block subsidy | Maximum newly issued amount a coinbase MAY claim at a height, excluding transaction fees |
| Rounding rule | Integer binary right shift; values below one base unit become zero |
| First later halving height | `2730000` |
| First zero-subsidy height | `63630000` |

The phase anchor is used only to calculate subsidy at and above the activation
height. It does not make the extended-epoch rule retroactive and does not alter
the validity of any historical block.

# Pre-Activation Rule

For every block height $h < 840000$, conforming software MUST apply the
deployed pre-activation subsidy rule without modification. This specification
does not restate that rule as new normative text.

The inspected deployed implementation is `GetBlockSubsidy` at commit
`b52c87778f800dc5f4e2f59c372badbc139f933f`
[@rincoinCore2026subsidy].
The candidate implementation MUST demonstrate identical subsidy outputs and
block-validity behaviour below activation through regression tests.

# Activation

The candidate rule activates at **block height 840,000**.

- Height 839,999 MUST use the deployed pre-activation rule.
- Height 840,000 MUST use the S5/b post-activation calculation with phase
  index $n=0$.
- Height 840,001 MUST remain in phase index $n=0$.
- The phase anchor at height 630,000 MUST NOT be applied as a new rule to any
  height below 840,000.

There is no transition window in which either subsidy rule is accepted.

# Post-Activation Subsidy Rule

For block height $h \geq H$, calculate:

$$
n=\left\lfloor\frac{h-A}{L}\right\rfloor.
$$

The maximum permitted block subsidy is:

$$
\operatorname{Subsidy}(h)=
\begin{cases}
625{,}000{,}000 \mathbin{\mathtt{>>}} n, & 0\leq n<30,\\
0, & n\geq30.
\end{cases}
$$

The right shift is an integer operation on a non-negative value. An
implementation MUST test `n >= 30` before shifting so that it does not perform
an out-of-range shift.

This is binary integer halving, nominally a 50% reduction, with floor rounding
at base-unit precision. When the preceding value is odd, the effective
percentage reduction can differ slightly from 50%.

Consequences:

- height 840,000 returns `625000000` base units;
- height 2,729,999 returns `625000000` base units;
- height 2,730,000 returns `312500000` base units;
- each subsequent 2,100,000-block boundary applies the specified binary
  integer-halving operation;
- there is no fixed subsidy floor;
- there is no constant terminal phase;
- there is no perpetual tail emission;
- height 63,629,999 returns `1` base unit;
- height 63,630,000 and every later height return zero.

# Integer Arithmetic

A conforming implementation:

1. MUST represent subsidy in integer base units;
2. MUST calculate the phase index from integer block heights;
3. MUST use binary integer right shift or an exactly equivalent integer-only
   division by $2^n$;
4. MUST return zero when $n\geq30$ without performing an out-of-range shift;
5. MUST NOT use floating-point arithmetic in consensus calculation;
6. MUST produce the same result on every supported architecture and build
   configuration.

Conceptual pseudocode:

```cpp
CAmount GetPost840kS5BSubsidy(int height)
{
    assert(height >= 840000);

    const int64_t phase =
        ((int64_t)height - 630000) / 2100000;

    if (phase >= 30) {
        return 0;
    }
    return ((CAmount)625000000) >> phase;
}
```

An equivalent implementation MAY be used only if exhaustive phase tests
demonstrate identical subsidy outputs and block-validity behaviour.

# Issuance Accounting

The maximum permitted subsidy MUST be a deterministic function of block height.
It MUST NOT depend on:

- actual subsidy claimed by earlier coinbase transactions;
- circulating, spendable, active, lost, or burned supply;
- UTXO state beyond ordinary block validation;
- market price or network hashrate;
- transaction fees.

The total value of coinbase outputs MUST NOT exceed the maximum permitted block
subsidy at height $h$ plus the transaction fees collected from that block.

Transaction fees are transfers of existing RIN and are not newly issued supply.
A miner MAY claim less than the maximum permitted subsidy. Any underclaimed
amount MUST NOT be reissued at a later height.

# Maximum Scheduled Issuance

Under the candidate integer rule:

- maximum scheduled issuance below height 840,000 is
  `19,687,500.00000000 RIN`;
- maximum scheduled issuance at and above height 840,000 is
  `24,937,499.76900000 RIN`;
- total maximum scheduled issuance is
  **`44,624,999.76900000 RIN`**;
- the first zero-subsidy height is **`63,630,000`**.

The original whitepaper's 168,000,000 RIN statement is a historical upper
design bound, not the effective maximum of this rule. No state-dependent
mechanism can increase scheduled issuance from 44,624,999.76900000 RIN toward
168,000,000 RIN.

These totals assume every block claims the maximum permitted subsidy. Actual
issued and circulating supply MAY be lower.

# Compatibility and Activation Risk

At height 840,000, S5/b permits `6.25000000 RIN`, while the unchanged deployed
binary-halving rule permits `3.12500000 RIN`. S5/b therefore has no immediate
miner-revenue shock, but consensus activation divergence is immediate. A block
whose coinbase claims more than the legacy amount but no more than the S5/b
amount will be valid under S5/b and invalid under unchanged software.

Nodes enforcing different rules can therefore diverge at or after the first
block whose coinbase claim distinguishes the rules. Deployment MUST be treated
as a hard fork. Implementers MUST test:

- height 839,999 and 840,000 boundary behaviour;
- heights 2,729,999 and 2,730,000;
- coinbase claims below, equal to, and one base unit above each maximum;
- reorganisation across the activation boundary in both directions;
- initial block download across the boundary;
- block-template subsidy and miner coinbase validation;
- deterministic behaviour on all supported platforms.

# Chain Identification and Replay

This subsidy change separates block validity but does not, by itself, prevent
transaction replay between branches that share transaction formats and
signature rules. A block-version marker alone would not provide transaction
replay protection.

Before activation readiness is claimed, a separate deployment analysis MUST
resolve or explicitly accept:

- P2P and software identity;
- wallet and service chain selection;
- explorer and exchange labelling;
- deposit and withdrawal routing;
- transaction replay exposure;
- whether replay protection requires an additional consensus change.

# Non-Normative Rationale

The companion *Rincoin Monetary Policy and Security Scenario Analysis* compares
S5/b against S1, the unchanged rule, other extended-epoch schedules, fixed
phases, cap-derived decline, Customized Halving study schedules, and perpetual
tails. The *Rincoin Monetary Review Summary* presents the decision path and
questions for public review [@rincoinAnalysis2026; @rincoinReviewSummary2026].

S5/b allocates the remaining issuance through approximately four-year binary
integer halvings, nominally 50%, and avoids an immediate miner-revenue reduction
at activation. It is one member of the principal comparison pair in the
public-review package; S1 allocates almost the same final issuance through
recursive 19/20 reductions, nominally 5%. This rationale is non-normative and
does not alter any requirement in this specification.
